window_frame.note: Commodore's own Figure 3-3 shows a whole Workbench disk window for this exact release, from the title strip through both scrollers to the sizing gadget. It is a screen dump printed in halftone, so the frame's anatomy is settled but its one-pixel relief is not resolvable; the emulator capture beside it is resampled to 1241x747 and carries over a thousand colours, so it cannot supply 1x geometry either.

title_bar.note: Figure 3-3 preserves the full title strip: close gadget hard against the leading edge, disk name with percentage full, free and in-use byte counts, then the zoom and depth gadgets at the trailing edge. Demoted from measured because neither source gives native pixels: the print is halftoned and the emulator capture is resampled.

window_buttons.note: Figure 3-3 is annotated by Commodore with the gadget names, so the close, zoom, depth and sizing roles and their positions are certain. Exact plate sizes are not: the halftone dissolves the one-pixel bevels at 600 dpi, which is why this is no longer measured.

toolbar.note: Workbench 3.1 has no general Finder-style toolbar; Threading keeps command rows in Intuition button material.

buttons.note: The file requester's OK, Volumes, Parent and Cancel row and the Format window's Format, Quick Format and Cancel row both show native action gadgets in their resting state. The manual's Action Gadgets section names the standard set (Save, Use, Cancel, OK, Retry, Continue, Help); no pressed-state figure is printed.

choice_controls.note: Figure 4-5 shows four native checkboxes in one column, one ticked, two empty and one ghosted, beside their right-aligned labels. Cycle and radio gadgets appear only as small marginal glyphs on printed pages 3-11, too small to measure.

fields.note: Figure 3-5 shows a string gadget carrying the selected text EMPTY with its block cursor, and a ghosted New Name label; the file requester adds Drawer and File gadgets at rest. Caret and selection colours are not recoverable from a black-and-white print.

menus.note: Figure 2-3 finally supplies an open pull-down: the Workbench, Window and Icons menu bar with the Workbench menu dropped, seven items, right-aligned Amiga-key shortcuts, an ellipsis marking items that open a requester, and no separator rules. The pointer sits over Backdrop but no item is drawn selected, so the highlight state is still unrecorded. The emulator capture's top strip was dropped from this component: it is the Workbench screen title bar, which is what the menu bar replaces while the menu button is held, not a menu.

popovers.note: Workbench has no anchored popover idiom; Threading should use a compact square requester-like information card.

scrollbars.note: Figure 3-3 is annotated with scroll bar, scroll gadget and scroll arrows, and shows the horizontal proportional gadget, the arrow pair at the trailing end, and the sizing gadget sharing the bottom rail; the file requester's Figure 3-6 adds a vertical scroller with its own arrow pair below the trough. The emulator pixels identify the proportional gadget as the same #6688BB blue used by the active title strip; production now derives that fill from the authored chrome rather than the darker general action accent. Native one-pixel relief remains unresolved.

lists_tables.note: Figure 3-6 preserves a native scrolling list: file names left, sizes right-aligned, dates in a third column, and ghosted drawer rows below the files, with the scroller seated inside the list border.

progress.note: Commodore documents the component in prose without printing it. Copying a disk shows a horizontal bar gauge of the percentage completed (printed page 4-9), and formatting opens a window showing the percentage formatted with a Stop gadget to cancel (printed page 4-17). No figure of either window has been found, so nothing can be measured yet.

alerts_toasts.note: Figure 3-4 preserves a whole native action requester, the DiskCopy Request: title strip with a depth gadget, framed message well with two lines of Topaz, and Continue and Cancel gadgets bookending the bottom rail. The manual also records the keyboard shortcuts, left Amiga+V to proceed and left Amiga+B to cancel. Production ThemedAlert now consumes the same classic requester grammar for Workbench: application-gray floating surface, hard relief, compact unsmoothed Topaz copy, and no modern status symbol. The printed figure is halftone, so the title-strip and one-pixel requester relief remain source-shaped rather than measured.

typography.note: The Format window's label column is the cleanest Topaz specimen in the manual, and the title strip and list rows repeat it. It is a print reproduction at roughly 3.7x the screen, so glyph shapes and the monospaced cell are legible while exact stem weights are not.

icons.note: Figure 3-3 preserves the eight standard Workbench drawer icons with their labels below, plus the Prefs drawer's distinct question-mark artwork. The emulator capture supplies their colours; the manual supplies their shapes.

reproductions.note: Production WindowTitleBandView at the compact 18px Workbench strip, retaining the active blue, split close/zoom/depth placement, a source-shaped disk-usage title, and the bundled GPL-FE Topaz 2.x/3.1 face in its native regular weight with antialiasing disabled. The 18px band and 18x16 gadget slots follow the proportions visible in the resampled emulator crop and manual figure; Commodore's linked figure is still halftone/resampled, so this remains an anatomy and glyph-shape review rather than an exact pixel reconstruction.

Production 18x16 WindowChromeButton gadgets in normal, restored, and pressed states. Now linked to Commodore's own annotated gadget pair rather than the resampled emulator capture; the reference is a halftone print, so this stays a shape comparison rather than an exact reconstruction.

Production ThemedAlert rendered with the source action-requester title strip, depth gadget, compact unsmoothed Topaz copy, gray body well, and Continue/Cancel bookends. The manual figure is a halftone print, so this is a source-shaped review fixture rather than a native-pixel equality claim.

Production ThemedScrollView family fixture, linked to the manual's annotated bottom rail so the proportional gadget, arrow pair and sizing gadget can be compared as a group. Its proportional gadget follows the authored active title blue (#6688BB for stock Workbench). Native-pixel relief evidence is still missing, so this remains a 2× review aid.

Production ThemedMenu surface with all seven source items, ellipses, a true aligned key-equivalent column, theme-owned Amiga-key caps, and the unsmoothed Topaz menu raster path. The Commodore figure is a magnified halftone print, so the review establishes grammar and glyph shapes rather than claiming native-pixel equality.

Production ThemedButton row carrying the file requester's four source labels and Workbench's square two-ring relief. The manual crop is a magnified halftone print, so widths are source-shaped rather than asserted as native-pixel measurements.

Production ThemedCheckbox column reproducing the source's checked, empty and ghosted states with compact sunken gadgets, a one-bit mark and unsmoothed Topaz labels instead of accent fills or SF Symbols.

Production ThemedTextField and Topaz prompt arranged like Commodore's Rename requester. The field keeps AppKit editing semantics while its recessed four-colour surface and resting text are drawn by the design system.
